value.answer: For most adults, short-term use at low doses (5 mg or less) looks safe. The usual side effects are mild, like headache and drowsiness, and they go away when you stop. Long-term safety isn't well established yet. A preliminary AHA study from November 2025 linked 12+ months of use in people with insomnia to higher heart failure risk, but it isn't peer-reviewed and can't prove cause. A later 2026 analysis found no significant link, so it's still an open question. Don't take it long-term without a proper reason from your doctor. If you take blood thinners or antidepressants, check with a doctor or pharmacist before using it.
